title: Layered universal-tableau execution
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean multi-tape Turing machine, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input word, and let $n,z,T,p$ be natural numbers with $1\le T$. The eleven-register counter program constructed from $M$, run on $x$, has a run of at most $(T+1)(\mathrm{layerBound}(n,z,T)+7T+10)$ steps from its layer-start label with the register values specified by $\mathrm{lstart}(0,0)$ and input position $p$ to the label for the final template, with register values specified by $\mathrm{lstart}(T+1,0)$ and the same input position; the output appended during this run is the concatenation, over indices $i=0,\ldots,(T+1)\mathrm{Str}(n,z,T)-1$, of the instruction-bit strings for index $i$.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $p$ representing the input position
